title: How a tenant profile is enforced: the headers ZIA inserts

microsoft-headers.statement: When a tenant profile is associated with a Cloud App Control rule and a request reaches login.microsoftonline.com, login.microsoft.com, login.windows.net or login.live.com, ZIA inserts `Restrict-Access-Context` (the Tenant Directory ID) and `Restrict-Access-To-Tenants` (the Office 365 Tenants or Tenant IDs). It inserts `sec-Restrict-Tenant-Access-Policy` only for login.live.com traffic, and only when Allow Personal Office 365 Domains is No.

quotes: The Zscaler service inserts the following headers when a tenant profile is associated with the Cloud App Control policy rule and there is an incoming request to login.microsoftonline.com, login.microsoft.com, login.windows.net, or login.live.com:
The value of the Tenant Directory ID field is inserted into this header.
The values of the Office 365 Tenants or Tenant IDs field are inserted into this header.
The value of the Allow Personal Office 365 Domains field is inserted into this header only for login.live.com traffic when the field is set to No.

google-header.statement: For any google.com request (or associated Google app), ZIA adds `X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains` carrying the profile's Domains. Google apps that need no sign-in, such as Google search, are unaffected, but a user who signs in from Google search with an account that is not on the allowlist is blocked.

quotes: The service intercepts any google.com (or associated Google app) request and adds the HTTP header X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains (values of the Domains field)
This feature does not affect Google apps that do not require users to sign in, such as Google search.
But a user who signs in from Google search with an account that is not placed on the allowlist is blocked.

chatgpt-header.statement: For requests to chatgpt.com and its subdomains, ZIA adds `ChatGPT-Allowed-Workspace-Id` carrying the profile's workspace IDs.

quotes: The service intercepts requests related to chatgpt.com and its subdomain (*chatgpt.com) and adds the HTTP header ChatGPT-Allowed-Workspace-Id (values of the Workspace ID for ChatGPT field).

claude-header.statement: For requests to claude.ai, claude.com and anthropic.com, ZIA adds `anthropic-allowed-org-ids` carrying the profile's workspace IDs.

quotes: The service intercepts requests related to Claude (claude.ai and claude.com) and Anthropic (anthropic.com) and adds the HTTP header anthropic-allowed-org-ids (values of the Workspace ID for Claude field).

docusign-header.statement: For requests to docusign.com or docusign.net, ZIA adds `X-Docusign-Allow-Organization` carrying the profile's account IDs.

quotes: The service intercepts requests related to docusign.com or docusign.net and adds the HTTP header X-Docusign-Allow-Organization (values of the Account ID for Docusign field).

dropbox-header.statement: For Dropbox requests, ZIA adds `X-Dropbox-allowed-Team-Ids` carrying the profile's team IDs. Network control must be enabled in Dropbox for tenancy restriction.

quotes: The service intercepts requests related to Dropbox and adds the HTTP header X-Dropbox-allowed-Team-Ids (values of the Dropbox Team ID field).
You must enable network control for tenancy restriction.

ibm-header.statement: For requests to cloud.ibm.com and its subdomains, ZIA adds `IBM-Cloud-Tenant` carrying the profile's IBM account IDs.

quotes: The service intercepts incoming requests to cloud.ibm.com and its subdomain (*cloud.ibm.com) and adds the HTTP header IBM-Cloud-Tenant (values of the IBM Account IDs field).

slack-headers.statement: For Slack requests, ZIA adds `X-Slack-Allowed-Workspaces-Requester` (the Your Workspace ID) and `X-Slack-Allowed-Workspaces` (the Allowed Workspace IDs).

quotes: The service intercepts requests related to Slack and adds the following headers:
X-Slack-Allowed-Workspaces-Requester (value of the Your Workspace ID field)
X-Slack-Allowed-Workspaces (values of the Allowed Workspace ID field)

webex-header.statement: For incoming requests to the Webex identity hosts (identity.webex.com, identity-eu.webex.com, idbroker.webex.com, idbroker-secondary.webex.com, idbroker-b-us.webex.com, idbroker-eu.webex.com, atlas-a.wbx2.com), ZIA adds `CiscoSpark-Allowed-Domains` carrying the profile's Webex tenants.

quotes: The service intercepts incoming requests to the following domains and adds the HTTP header CiscoSpark-Allowed-Domains (values of the Webex Tenants(Webex Teams and Meetings) field):
idbroker-secondary.webex.com
atlas-a.wbx2.com

github-zoom-header-names.statement: The Help form ties the GitHub field to the `sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise` header and the Zoom Policy Label to the `X-ZoomApps-Policy` header. For these two it does not say that ZIA inserts the header, or on which hosts.

quotes: associated with the sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise header for GitHub.
enter the policy label associated with the X-ZoomApps-Policy header for Zoom.

github-zoom-header-names.conditions: The field descriptions name the header; the interception sentences that the other applications have are absent for GitHub and Zoom.

header-insertion.statement: ZIA conveys the tenant constraint by inserting the SaaS vendor's own tenant-restriction request header into the inspected request; the vendor then decides. This is documented for nine applications; it is not documented for AWS, Google Cloud Platform, YouTube or Zoho.
header-insertion.conditions: Generalized from the nine applications whose interception sentence names an inserted header. The decision being made by the vendor is inferred from the headers being the vendors' own.

needs-decrypted-traffic.statement: Header insertion into HTTPS needs the request decrypted, so a tenant restriction can work only where the SSL/TLS inspection rule covers the login service.
needs-decrypted-traffic.conditions: Inference: an inserted header cannot be added to a request ZIA cannot read. The Help text states the inspection requirement, not this reason.

per-app-inspection-detail.title: How ZIA enforces tenant restriction for the applications whose header is not documented
per-app-inspection-detail.detail: AWS, Google Cloud Platform, YouTube and Zoho Login Services have no inserted header or interception sentence in the captured Help article, and GitHub and Zoom name a header without saying ZIA inserts it. Whether these use header insertion, parameter inspection, or another detection model is not stated. Per-app configuration guides that may state it are not captured.
per-app-inspection-detail.blocks: explaining how tenant restriction is detected for AWS, GCP, YouTube and Zoho

bypassed-traffic-behavior.title: What tenant restriction does when the login service is bypassed from SSL inspection
bypassed-traffic-behavior.detail: The Help article requires SSL/TLS inspection for these applications but does not say whether a bypassed login flow passes without the restriction, is blocked, or fails some other way. For the general effect of bypass, see zia.ssl-inspection.bypass-impact.
bypassed-traffic-behavior.blocks: telling an operator whether a missing inspection rule fails open
